sections.overview: Mnemiopsis leidyi is a transparent, lobed comb jelly native to the Atlantic coasts of the Americas.
sections.identification: Its oval body is usually a few centimetres long and bears rows of beating cilia that shimmer in light; unlike true jellyfish, it is a ctenophore.
sections.habitat: It lives in the water column of estuaries, bays and shallow coastal waters, tolerating broad salinity and temperature changes.
sections.diet: It consumes zooplankton and can also eat eggs and larvae of pelagic fish, competing with young fish for planktonic food.
sections.behavior: When food is abundant it can form dense aggregations; its comb rows refract light and may appear to glow.
sections.reproduction: Each individual has male and female reproductive organs and can self-fertilize; under favorable conditions it matures and reproduces rapidly.
sections.ecology: Transported in ships’ ballast water, it spread beyond its native Atlantic range; blooms in the Black and Caspian seas disrupted plankton food webs and fisheries.
sections.conservation: Its effects differ by sea; Mediterranean impacts are reported as less dramatic than Black or Caspian Sea impacts.
